Slide Over engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume iPad Slide Over support covers storefront language. Xcode, entitlements, and Connect actually separate in-app multitasking behavior from product-page copy:

  • UIScene & Slide Over window scenes — configured in your app to appear in the narrow overlay strip and participate in edge-swipe multitasking. Controls runtime Slide Over behavior. Does not generate Chinese listing text. AppLocale does not implement this.
  • iPad multitasking entitlements & size classes — scene support, window scenes, and layout rules that determine whether your app opens in Slide Over or full screen. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Slide Over value to buyers.
  • In-app strip chrome & shelf labels — toolbar titles, compact panel labels, and switch-app affordances inside the Slide Over strip. Your listing may mention side shelf; implementing scene multitasking is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Slide Over support in the binary.

Working Slide Over in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Slide Over-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Slide Over–centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe the edge overlay strip — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Slide Over vs 侧拉 vs 滑入式多任务

US pages use "Slide Over", "Side shelf", "Swipe from edge", or "App Switcher shelf." Chinese buyers expect concise 侧拉, 滑入, or 滑入式多任务 phrasing rather than English slogans left on screenshot overlays — without implying you are the built-in multitasking system or support Slide Over in size classes your app does not ship.

Slide Over strip vs Split View panes

Slide Over marketing describes the narrow companion panel that floats over a full-screen app — one app dominant, one app in the edge strip. Split View marketing describes equal side-by-side columns with a draggable divider. Chinese buyers expect 侧拉 vocabulary (侧拉参考, 边缘小窗) rather than 分屏 or 并排 when the frame shows the overlay strip, not two equal panes.

App Switcher shelf vs Stage Manager groups

Drag-from-shelf workflows to open Slide Over are classic iPad multitasking — dock, App Switcher shelf, edge swipe. That is different from Stage Manager resizable window groups and 台前调度 layouts. Chinese buyers expect shelf-and-strip vocabulary (从程序坞拖入侧拉, 切换侧拉应用) rather than windowing badges (自由调整窗口) when the frame shows the narrow strip, not overlapping freeform windows.

Switch apps inside Slide Over vs Picture in Picture

Some Slide Over screenshots show switching between apps inside the narrow strip — Messages in Slide Over while Safari stays full screen. That is an app-panel multitasking story, not floating video. Chinese buyers expect 侧拉应用切换 vocabulary rather than 画中画 or 小窗播放 when the frame shows app chrome, not a video player corner window.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Slide Over search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 侧拉, 滑入, and iPad 多任务 each signal different intent from generic iPad productivity keywords or Split View 分屏 terms.

Screenshot captions on Slide Over frames

Gallery frames that show the narrow strip, App Switcher shelf drag targets, or switch-apps-inside-Slide-Over mockups need one-line zh-Hans captions — "侧拉打开，主屏不中断" not "Slide Over" burned into the product page story.

FAQ

Does AppLocale implement UIScene, Slide Over window scenes, or iPad multitasking engineering?

No. AppLocale rewrites App Store Connect metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, and screenshot caption lines on your zh-Hans product page. UIScene multitasking configuration and Slide Over window scene support are engineering tasks outside AppLocale scope.

How should zh-Hans listing copy talk about Slide Over without over-claiming?

Listing copy should describe the Slide Over flows your app actually ships — companion strip alongside a full-screen app, App Switcher shelf drag, switch apps inside the strip — without implying you replace system Slide Over, guarantee the overlay in every size class, or support Split View side-by-side panes when your app only runs in the narrow strip. We rewrite from your English source claims; we do not invent multitasking features your binary does not support.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans Slide Over listing fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters on the zh-Hans row. The keyword field allows up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially subtitle and caption lines that must fit on-device mockups showing the narrow Slide Over strip or App Switcher shelf.

How is this different from Split View, Stage Manager, or Picture in Picture guides?

Slide Over listing copy covers the narrow edge overlay strip — swipe from edge, side shelf, App Switcher shelf, switch apps inside Slide Over. Split View covers equal side-by-side panes. Stage Manager covers 台前调度 freeform windowing. Picture in Picture covers floating video windows. Those surfaces have separate listing guides.

No. iPad Slide Over at runtime comes from your app binary and system behavior — not App Store Connect listing fields. AppLocale covers product-page marketing copy only.
